subject: Dedicated sizing clarifications + sample telemetry request
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@embera.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing kickoff - initial traffic & questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking time to speak yesterday. As promised, I'm sending over a short primer on Embera's inference characteristics and an early ask so your team can size a pilot. Top-line: our product serves personalized recommendations + short completions (average prompt 45 tokens, avg response 220 tokens), with peak bursts during north-american business hours.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm what telemetry format you prefer for token/session sampling? (CSV, JSONL etc)
- How do you map session affinity vs. concurrency for Dedicated?
- Any guidance on GPU SKUs you recommend for mixed workflows (dense completions + reranking)?

I attached a small sample of sessions and a token distribution CSV. We're targeting a small pilot (50 qps sustained with 250 qps bursts) and want a proposal for a reserved fleet footprint + rough cost ballpark.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Head of Infrastructure
Embera Systems

Attachments: session_samples.jsonl (2.4MB), sample_token_trace.csv (120KB), embera_arch_overview.pdf (800KB)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@embera.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff - initial traffic & questions

Hi Amit — great primer, thanks.

We prefer JSONL for session samples (one event per line) but CSV is fine for simple token histograms — appreciate you sending both. I took a quick pass through the sample and have a few follow-ups to make the sizing reliable:

1) Prompt/response composition: are the 220 tokens mostly model-generated or do you have post-processing that expands these?
2) Burst profile: can you share a 24-hour token/time bucket (e.g., 1-min buckets for a 24h window) for a representative weekday?
3) Session affinity: do sessions require KV cache warm-starts (i.e., long-lived sessions with chat history persisted) or are they mostly stateless?

Marissa and Karthik — I started a lightweight intake below for the team to fill; could you take point on mapping these to a GPU mix (types, oversubscription, and a conservative recommended reserve) and return a draft by EOD Thursday? I'm especially interested in guidance for balancing A100-style instances vs. more cost-efficient L4/RTX-like SKUs for a mixed workload.

Proposed next steps to Amit:
- You provide the 24h bucketed trace + confirmation about KV cache shapes (JSONL preferred).
- We run a short profiling pass (lightload) and return a 2-tier Dedicated footprint: pilot (sized for burst tolerance) and scale plan (3-month commit).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30m lab walkthrough with Marissa to show how we map token flows to fleet shapes.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Amit Shah <amit@embera.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T13:45:00-07:00

Chloe — thanks, that works. Quick answers inline: 

- The 220 tokens are model-generated; we do a small sanitization step which adds negligible tokens.
- I'll export a 24h 1-min bucketed token/time trace and attach as JSONL by EOD.
- Session affinity: ~12% of requests are long-lived sessions (history kept, KV cache beneficial); the rest are short-lived stateless calls.

We'd love the pilot footprint. Meeting: Thursday 10am PT works for Marissa walkthrough.

—Amit
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Embera sizing - quick mapping

Marissa / Karthik — Amit confirmed: 50 qps sustained, 250 qps burst (short windows), avg prompt 45 tokens, avg response 220 tokens, ~12% sessions with affinity. He'll provide 1-min bucketed token traces.

Could you run a conservative mapping exercise:
- Baseline pilot: capacity to handle 250 qps bursts at p95 latency target (<= 400ms for short completions, <= 1s for long completions) with 20% headroom.
- SKU recommendations: list 2 options (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) with GPU counts, expected concurrency per GPU, and suggested oversubscription multipliers.
- KV/cache considerations: propose session pool sizing to support 12% affinity without degrading cold-start P95.

Draft the note as a short bulleted one-pager; we'll iterate before sharing externally. Target: Thursday 9/9 EOD internal draft.

Thanks — Chloe
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@embera.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-09-10T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff - initial traffic & questions

Amit — quick update and a tentative pilot footprint based on the samples you shared and our conservative profiling:

Summary of findings from sample: average token payload aligns with your numbers; peak 1-min buckets hit ~230 qps in the 24h sample. KV-affinity observed in ~11–13% of sessions.

Redwood recommended pilot (two options):

1) Latency-optimized (lower p95)
- GPUs: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (reserved)
- Expected sustained concurrency: ~60 concurrent short sessions per GPU with dynamic batching; p95 completion latency target ~300–350ms for short completions
- Oversubscription: conservative (0.8x) to preserve latency during burst windows

2) Cost-optimized (balanced throughput/cost)
- GPUs: 6 x L4-style 48GB-equivalent nodes
- Expected sustained concurrency: ~90 concurrent short sessions per GPU with slightly higher p95 (~450–600ms)
- Oversubscription: 1.2x during sustained windows, with auto-burst headroom for short spikes

KV/session pool recommendation:
- Maintain a warmed pool sized to cover ~15% of active sessions (slightly above observed) — suggest a small set of pinned warm slots (approx. 60 warm slots across the pilot cluster) to avoid cold KV penalties.

Next steps:
- If you prefer, Marissa can run a lightweight perf run on a synthetic trace to validate these numbers (30–60m).
- We can produce a 3-month ramp plan and pricing once you pick a preferred SKU direction.

Would you like us to schedule the Marissa walkthrough next week (Thu 10am PT) as proposed?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
